what_now_passes_and_what_does_not.why: crystallisation runs compile_and_qualify_skill, whose transfer-ownership gate returns COMPUTER_EXECUTION_REQUIRES_ADMITTED_CONFINEMENT. The gate will not persist a skill whose demonstration was executed outside the carrier, and _qualify_cli_measurement_skill's held-out and postcondition checks still use computer_env_v1.answer_query, which runs host programs unconfined.
what_now_passes_and_what_does_not.the_gate_is_right: a learned skill is the thing that will be trusted forever. Learning it from an unconfined execution would make the permanence permanent over a proof that was never admitted. Refusing is the correct behaviour and I did not override it.
what_now_passes_and_what_does_not.so_the_honest_position_is: the question is ANSWERED correctly under confinement, and it is NOT YET LEARNED. Those are different claims and only the first one is now true.
